rationale: The authored three-row giving rule agrees internally with the cited Lean relations. Give.move combines unique effective resolution with Take and returns the same object under a unique reference while emptying the final slot. Give.copy combines shared effective resolution with an already-shared stored reference and preserves the state. Give.promote combines shared effective resolution with Promote, changing exactly the final unique occurrence to shared before returning a shared copy of the same object. Mode.join propagates any shared link through later projections; the distinct-key convention in shared.state makes the selected storage slot unambiguous. Thus I found no prose-to-Lean mismatch in the implemented lazy final-slot promotion rule. However, extra:reviews/adversarial-2026-10-24/design-context.md records a known unresolved intended-design choice: the user required shared-copy behavior after traversing a shared link, while the alternatives of final-slot promotion, whole-subtree promotion, and access-path-based exclusivity were raised and remained unanswered. The implementation selected the first provisionally. The policy requires an inconclusive result or mismatch when intended design is ambiguous. Mutual agreement of the chosen prose and implementation cannot resolve that recorded alternative, and the earlier positive record explicitly limited itself to the provisional choice. Inconclusive is appropriate because no supplied intent rules out lazy promotion, but the intended changes to stored modes have not been resolved. Resolve and preserve that design choice as review input, or establish an appropriate observational equivalence among representations, before treating this unit as positively reviewed against intended design. This conclusion does not impose a general human-approval requirement: the issue is the specific known ambiguity, not merely absence of human approval.
limitations: The pending issue is intended ownership-mode behavior. The existing lazy implementation is internally coherent; this review does not establish that an alternative implementation is required or that current Lean preservation or embedding theorems are false.

The design-history premise comes from the recoverable added context input with its stated primary-agent provenance. I did not independently authenticate the underlying conversation. A correction or explicit resolution of that context requires a new comparison.

This review does not claim an observational equivalence between lazy and eager promotion or access-path-based exclusivity, nor that the Given-to-Shared embedding settles the choice: that embedded fragment does not exercise sharing.

The listed source contexts were inspected for relevant definitions and concrete behaviors. This record is not a complete tactic audit, proof-build report, source-language progress proof, or validator-correctness assessment.
